scenes.narration: Narrate turns a plain JSON script into a fully narrated, timed explainer video on Apple Silicon.

visual.headline: How Narrate Works
visual.sub: From JSON script to local speech and deterministic video

scenes.narration: Every video runs through four stages: validate the script, synthesize speech locally, align word timings, and render frames with Remotion.
At the core, the schema feeds a single visual registry that dispatches each scene to either its two-dimensional or three-dimensional view.
During audio generation, the CLI sends narration to Kokoro, receives per-word timestamps, and writes a timing manifest that drives every reveal.
Zooming out, the full build loop validates the script, loops back on errors, skips synthesis on cache hits, and renders the final video.

visual.heading: Full Build & Cache Loop
visual.code:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Input

  end

  E --> S
  V -->|yes| C{Audio Cached?}
  subgraph Pipeline
    C -->|no| T[Kokoro Speech]
    T --> A[Word Timings]
    C -->|yes| A
    A --> R[Remotion Render]
  end
  R --> M[Final Video]
visual.caption: Subgraphs, validation feedback loop, and cache bypass

scenes.narration: Both rendering modes share the exact same script format: two-dimensional mode maximizes diagram density, while three-dimensional mode adds spatial depth.
And the final callout: write your story once, and switch between two-dimensional and three-dimensional rendering with a single mode field.

visual.heading: Key Takeaway
visual.text: Same narration, same timings, same cel-sky theme.
